artists.biography:
Killing Joke are an English post-punk band formed in October 1978 in Notting Hill, London, England; other sources report the band formed in early 1979. Founding members Jaz Coleman (vocals, keyboards) and Geordie Walker (guitars) have been the only constant members.
A key influence on industrial rock, their early music was described by critics Stephen Thomas Erlewine and John Dougan as "quasi-metal ... dancing to a tune of doom and gloom", which gradually evolved over the years, incorporating elements of electronic music, synthpop, gothic rock, and alternative rock, though always emphasising Coleman's "savagely strident vocals".
Finding modest commercial success, Killing Joke have influenced many later bands and artists, such as Nirvana, Ministry, Amen, Lamb of God, Nine Inch Nails, Porcupine Tree, Napalm Death, Behemoth, Amebix, Big Black, Slipknot, Opeth, Murderdolls, Godflesh, Scorn, Hole/Courtney Love, Dead by April, Marilyn Manson, Tool, Prong, Metallica, Primus, Jane's Addiction, Soundgarden, Foo Fighters, Faith No More, Nick Harper, Blacklist, Shihad, Pitchshifter, Das Oath, Rammstein, and Korn, all of whom have at some point cited some debt of gratitude to Killing Joke.

perplexity.description:
The Singles Collection 1979-2012 by Killing Joke is a comprehensive anthology that spans over three decades of the band's influential output, originally released in 2012 through Spinefarm Records. This compilation showcases the band's evolution across genres such as electronic, rock, and pop, featuring 33 singles that highlight their pioneering post-punk and industrial sound. Key tracks include early anthems like "Wardance" and "Nervous System," as well as later hits such as "Love Like Blood," "Millennium," and "Pandemonium," reflecting their blend of aggressive guitar work, electronic textures, and rhythmic intensity.

Positioned as a definitive singles collection, this release captures Killing Joke’s consistent ability to innovate and remain relevant from their late 1970s origins through the early 2010s. The album serves both as an accessible entry point for new listeners and a detailed archival resource for longtime fans, with editions ranging from a standard multi-CD set to an extensive super-deluxe box featuring rarities and unreleased tracks. Critically, the collection has been praised for its breadth and the band's enduring influence on alternative and industrial music scenes, though some minor omissions were noted by reviewers. Commercially, it underscores Killing Joke’s status as a seminal band with a dedicated following, consolidating their legacy through a curated retrospective of their most impactful singles.
